Reading the July 26, 2017 FOMC statement alongside the July 2017 SLOOS nudges the tone modestly more dovish. While the Committee highlights solid job gains and a lower unemployment rate, the SLOOS reports broadly weaker loan demand in key categories (CRE, construction/land development, multifamily, and consumer credit including auto and credit cards) and tighter standards for consumer, auto, and credit card loans. Foreign banks also reported tighter standards for C&I and CRE. Easing in residential mortgage standards (including jumbo, QM, and GSE) and unchanged standards for some home-purchase/HELOC segments partially offset these headwinds, but the net SLOOS signal points to softer credit demand/availability. Combined with inflation running below 2 percent and low market-based inflation compensation, these SLOOS findings reinforce a cautious, gradual policy path and a slightly more dovish tilt than the statement alone.
